exposure: Cervical ripening method (balloon catheter vs. prostaglandins)
cohort: 74 women with a singleton fetus in breech presentation at ≥ 37 weeks gestation, with an unfavorable cervix, who underwent cervical ripening for a medical indication
finding: The study found no significant difference in cesarean delivery rates, neonatal morbidity, or mortality between mechanical (balloon catheter) and pharmaceutical (prostaglandins) methods of cervical ripening in women with a singleton fetus in breech presentation at term.
